text:
jamie: quick q — running into 401s when streaming with the Node SDK. header looks like `Authorization: Basic <token>` but server rejects. set via env var in CI. anyone seen this?

nina: do you suspect trailing newline? CI runners sometimes add \n when echoing secrets into env.

jamie: possible. how to check quickly in CI? can't print the secret in logs.

ricardo: locally you can `printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | xxd` to spot a trailing 0a. note: `echo` adds newline, `echo -n` avoids it. on Windows `setx`/Notepad can introduce CRLF.

seb: also double-check the base64 step. Basic auth is usually base64(API_KEY + ':'). a stray newline changes the base64 string. quick node one-liner: `node -e \"console.log(Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64'))\"`

jamie: ah, i was using a GH Actions step that did `cat secret.txt` and then `echo \"API_KEY=$SECRET\" >> $GITHUB_ENV`. does that append a newline?

nina: GH actions will write a newline at EOF. use `printf 'API_KEY=%s' \"$SECRET\" >> $GITHUB_ENV` or strip on runtime: `API_KEY=${API_KEY%$'\n'}` to be safe.

ricardo: for Go clients i usually avoid generic TrimSpace (it can hide other whitespace). prefer `strings.TrimSuffix(apiKey, "\n")` and `TrimSuffix(..., "\r")` so you only remove what you expect.

jamie: testing now... was also seeing streaming retries fail with weird JSON parse errors — makes sense if the server rejected the auth and returned HTML error page mid-stream.

seb: quick curl check that bypasses SDK: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n $API_KEY: | base64)\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` should 200. if 401, run `echo -n $API_KEY | hexdump -C` to confirm trailing bytes.

devops-bot: Reminder: rotating API keys tonight at 22:00 UTC. if you're debugging auth, try the staging key to avoid lockouts.

jamie: :thumbsup: found it — CRLF from a Windows editor in the secret file in the repo. i added `tr -d '\r\n'` in the GH Actions step and streaming + retries work again. thanks all!
